system_description.narrative_title: Escalation around Iran-Houthi-Saudi conflict shocks oil markets
system_description.narrative_summary: A rapid escalation of Iran-backed Houthi attacks on Saudi targets and shipping in the Strait of Hormuz is reshaping regional security and global energy markets. The violence is generating immediate market shocks (oil at ~$110/bbl), prompting regional military posturing and external responses (Egypt, US, Europe), and exposing capability gaps that feed political and economic feedbacks. These dynamics create a reinforcing loop: attacks raise prices and disrupt investment/events, which in turn harden state responses and risk further escalation.
system_description.scope: Regional military and proxy confrontation centered on Iran, the Houthis, and Saudi Arabia; attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure (Strait of Hormuz, refineries, Aramco); immediate market and investor reactions (oil prices, refiner margins, conference postponements); state-level political/military responses from regional actors (Egypt, Qatar, Saudi) and external powers (US, Europe).
system_description.super_system: Global energy-security-economic system (interdependence of oil markets, international trade, and geopolitical stability)
adjacent_subsystems: Global oil markets and commodity trading
Gulf regional security architecture (Saudi-Iran rivalry, GCC dynamics)
Maritime security and shipping insurance/logistics (Strait of Hormuz transit)
evidence_headlines: Brent oil touches $110 as Iran escalates Hormuz attacks, Ukraine vows to hit Russian refineries
Iran Is Giving Houthis Targeting and Intelligence for Attacks on Saudi Arabia
Oil touches $110 a barrel for first time since May on Middle East, Russia supply fears
Egypt says ready to give Saudi Arabia necessary support amid Houthi conflict
Saudi Arabia postpones ‘Davos in the desert’ after Houthi attacks

variables.name: Oil price level
variables.description: The prevailing benchmark price level of crude oil measured on a continuous scale.

variables.name: Maritime security risk
variables.description: The aggregate risk of hostile incidents, attacks, or disruptions to commercial shipping in critical waterways.

variables.name: Shipping traffic flow
variables.description: The volume of commercial maritime transits through key chokepoints per unit time.

variables.name: Supply disruption extent
variables.description: The proportion of energy (oil and refined products) supply that is currently unavailable or curtailed relative to baseline.

variables.name: Refinery input cost pressure
variables.description: The level of upward pressure on refineries' feedstock acquisition costs and margin compression.

variables.name: Refinery throughput rate
variables.description: The aggregated rate at which refineries process crude into products over time.

variables.name: Investor risk perception
variables.description: The average market participant perception of geopolitical and market risk affecting investment decisions.

variables.name: Market volatility level
variables.description: The degree of short-term price fluctuation and uncertainty in energy and related financial markets.

variables.name: Strategic reserve release rate
variables.description: The rate at which strategic oil reserves are being drawn down and released into markets over time.

variables.name: Military posturing intensity
variables.description: The scale and visibility of military deployments, maneuvers, and readiness levels in the region.

variables.name: Proxy attack frequency
variables.description: The frequency of indirect or proxy armed actions directed at infrastructure, shipping, or territory per unit time.

variables.name: External intervention probability
variables.description: The perceived likelihood that outside actors will undertake formal military or major political intervention.

variables.name: Defense production capacity
variables.description: The available industrial capacity to produce, sustain, and replenish military matériel and munitions.

variables.name: Insurance premium level
variables.description: The prevailing level of insurance and war-risk premiums for maritime and energy-related transport.

variables.name: Energy investment rate
variables.description: The flow of capital into energy production, refining, and related infrastructure projects per unit time.

variables.name: Escalation feedback strength
variables.description: The intensity of reinforcing processes by which attacks, responses, and market reactions amplify further escalation.

catalysts.title: Escalation of attacks in the Strait of Hormuz
catalysts.description: A near-term intensification of mines, missile and strike incidents against tankers and cargo in the Strait of Hormuz, reducing safe transit and raising regional risk.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Iran's Guards say two tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz"; "Two Cargo Ships Sink Near Strait of Hormuz, as Iranian Attacks Increase".

catalysts.title: U.S. strategic reserve exchange solicitation / possible release
catalysts.description: U.S. solicitation to exchange up to 17 million barrels could lead to near-term strategic reserve draws or releases affecting global supply balances.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "US solicits exchange of up to 17 million barrels of oil from strategic reserve"; market headlines on prices and supply.

catalysts.title: Egypt parliamentary decision on backing Saudi military action
catalysts.description: Egypt's parliament may be asked to approve support for Saudi operations; a legislative authorization would enable more direct Egyptian involvement.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Egypt's Sisi seeks parliament's backing to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked"; "Egypt says ready to give Saudi Arabia necessary support amid Houthi conflict."

catalysts.title: Iran's 'new operational plan' and expanded Houthi support
catalysts.description: Iran signals and implements a new operational plan and provides targeting/intelligence to Houthis, likely increasing proxy operations against Saudi targets and shipping.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Iran says it has a 'new operational plan' if the U.S. resumes attacks"; "Iran Is Giving Houthis Targeting and Intelligence for Attacks on Saudi Arabia."

catalysts.title: Spike in attacks on Saudi energy and infrastructure
catalysts.description: Increased Houthi/ Iran-backed strikes against Saudi facilities and personnel, including a reported attack on Aramco headquarters, raising disruption risk to energy assets.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Houthis attack Saudi Aramco headquarters"; "Missiles hit Aden airport"; "Houthis encircle new target".

catalysts.title: Postponement of 'Davos in the Desert' and investor pause
catalysts.description: Saudi postponement of its major investor conference reduces near-term investor engagement and deal flow into regional energy projects.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Saudi Arabia to postpone ‘Davos in the desert’ after Houthi attacks"; "Saudi Arabia postpones big investor conference to 2027."

catalysts.title: War-risk and marine insurance premium spike
catalysts.description: War-risk and hull/war premiums and captain security surcharges rise sharply for Gulf transits, increasing transport costs and reroute incentives.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Ships’ captains paid $100,000 a month to transit Strait of Hormuz" and multiple shipping attack reports.

catalysts.title: Pakistan army chief visits Tehran
catalysts.description: Official Pakistani military visit to Tehran could alter regional diplomatic dynamics, either dampening or shifting alliances and interventions.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Pakistan army chief Asim Munir to visit Tehran on Tuesday."

catalysts.title: Risk of U.S. strike on Iran (Pickaxe Mountain rhetoric)
catalysts.description: Public threats referencing a possible strike raise the chance of U.S. kinetic action or escalatory signaling, heightening market and conflict risks.
catalysts.rationale: Cites: "Trump says US may need to strike Iran's Pickaxe Mountain" and Iran's warning about responses.
